newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to cut public deficit by 32 bln ffr in 1997.
newsitem.headline: France to cut public deficit by 32 bln ffr in 1997.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday the government would cut the 1997 public deficit by 32 billion francs.
"It concerns 0.4 percent of GDP," he said. "Less would have been insufficient, more would have blocked economic growth," he told a news conference.
He said the government planned 22 billion in tax measures in 1997, but added it did not plan additional taxes on households.
The remaining 10 billion francs would be achieved by central government spending cuts, of which two billion francs would come from the defence budget.
